items.title: Dopamine Budget · Product Owner / System Analyst
items.summary: Own the product end to end.
details: Own the product end to end: vision, scope, business rules, functional requirements, data model and architecture docs in Confluence.
Run the backlog in Jira: findings from a code review become prioritized tickets with a decision on each. Keep a decision log of what is built, postponed or rejected, and why.
Designed business processes in BPMN 2.0, user scenarios (main and alternative), an ER model, C4 and sequence diagrams.
Coordinate AI coding agents: I write requirements and acceptance criteria, agents implement, I accept and test the result.
For the first beta I switched off accounts and cloud sync because of privacy and GDPR risks: the app works offline.

caseStudy.title: Case study: Dopamine Budget
caseStudy.subtitle: An Android habit-tracking app I build as Product Owner, with AI agents as the dev team. Beta coming soon.

stories.title: A bug that was a missing requirement
stories.text: The sign-in button on the first onboarding slide was made for existing users. A new user who tapped it got an account and skipped the privacy slides. The code did what I asked: the path was never described.
stories.lesson: Lesson: for every flow, ask how else someone can get here.

stories.title: What lives on the server, what stays on the phone
stories.text: The app is offline-first. A four-question filter decides:
list: Will I change it after launch?
Does it exist only in sync mode?
What happens if the server is down?

stories.title: Cutting finished work for the beta
stories.text: For a real beta, I switched off accounts, cloud sync and other server features behind a build flag.
stories.lesson: “Done” and “ready to ship” are different things.

context.alt: Diagram. In the beta: the user logs habits in the Dopamine Budget Android app, which works offline and keeps all data on the phone; a home screen widget saves taps; reminders are scheduled on the phone. Switched off by a build flag: cloud backend, Google sign-in, push service.

userStory.title: User story: from story to task
userStory.story: As a new user, I want to see the privacy slides before any account is created, so that I decide what to share with full information.
userStory.why: The sign-in button on the first slide was made for existing users. A new user who tapped it got an account and skipped the privacy slides. The code did what I asked; the path was never described.
task: Slide order: A1 → A2 → A3 → B1 → B2 → B3 → B3m.
If tapping “Sign in” on A1 creates a new account, onboarding continues from A2, so no privacy slide is skipped.
Creating an account on B3 leads to B3m.
Step 1 is a recon: read the current flow before changing code.
Acceptance criteria and tests are part of the task.
userStory.short: As a user who cannot afford any of my habits today, I want to stop control for the day, so that I can honestly record a lapse.
gherkin: Given my balance is not enough for any habit
When I press the “Stop control” button
Then the day is marked as broken
And the habits screen is hidden
And the screen shows a supportive message

agentRules.title: How I brief AI agents
agentRules.intro: Rules I write into the sprint goal for the agent queue:
items: Read the project instructions file first.
If a question for the product owner is open, stop and ask. Do not guess.
Tests are mandatory, with a baseline: they were green before, they must be green after.
One commit per task, with the task key in the message.
Never touch production data or migrations.
